test.title: The long life of a bicycle

paragraphs.text: A steel frame from the 1970s can still be ridden today, while many frames sold now are expected to last a decade. Steel bends before it breaks and can be straightened; other materials crack.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Parts are the harder problem. A frame outlives three or four sets of wheels and brakes, and standards change so often that a ten-year-old bicycle may need parts that nobody makes.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Workshops that repair old machines have multiplied, often run as clubs where members pay a small fee and use the tools themselves under supervision.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Manufacturers have noticed the mood. Two companies now publish a list of parts they promise to supply for fifteen years, which they use in their advertising.
paragraphs.label: D
